name: Realtime app over WebSockets
summary: A web app whose screens update live: a WebSocket server fans out changes through Redis pub/sub to every connected client, with Postgres as the record. Chat, collaboration, dashboards and live tracking.

fitsWhen.says: the team writes TypeScript or Elixir

avoidWhen.says: only short-lived functions are allowed (sockets need long-lived processes)

frontend.why: Components re-render from socket events through a store.

backend.why: Node's event loop holds many idle sockets cheaply; Phoenix Channels (Elixir) or SignalR (.NET) are the swaps.

cache.why: Pub/sub fans a message out to every socket server; also presence and rate limits.

database.why: The durable record; sockets carry changes, the database keeps them.

auth.why: The socket handshake carries the session; authorise every channel join.

infra.why: Several socket servers behind a load balancer that supports WebSockets.

ci-cd.why: Tests and images on pull requests.

observability.why: Connected sockets, message rates and fan-out latency.

testing.why: Unit tests, two-browser Playwright tests, k6 for connection load.

services.name: web
responsibilities: Reconnects and resyncs after a drop

services.name: api
responsibilities: Publishes a change after each commit

services.name: realtime
responsibilities: Subscribes to the bus and forwards to the right rooms

dataStores.name: bus
dataStores.purpose: Pub/sub between API and socket servers; presence

environments.hosting: Two realtime instances to prove fan-out works

environments.name: prod
environments.hosting: Several realtime instances behind a WebSocket-aware load balancer

stages.name: test
stages.does: vitest; API tests with Postgres and Redis

stages.name: deploy

adrs.title: Fan-out through Redis pub/sub
adrs.decision: Socket servers subscribe to Redis channels.
adrs.why: Any number of socket servers stay in step without sticky sessions.

adrs.title: Write over HTTP, read live over sockets
adrs.decision: Writes go to the API; sockets only push.
adrs.why: Validation, auth and transactions stay in one place.
